sources.reason: Preparation validation uses the highest immutable remote semantic tag when checking the next candidate.
The pending v0.5.44 candidate must advance because v0.5.44 is already an immutable Draft tag.

executionDecision.reason: The user authorized a documented recovery Work Item in PR #401 because its archived predecessor is blocked by the release-candidate validation it repaired. This is a narrowly scoped serial recovery exception, not permission to alter archived evidence or bypass PR checks.

preReviewWarnings: Review public-release identity separately from immutable tag reservation; a Draft tag reserves its version but does not become the published baseline.

checkpointPolicy.reason: Record checkpoints around recovery metadata and guard changes.

acceptance: Preparation validation describes remote tags as immutable reserved tags rather than accepted public releases and still requires the candidate to be exactly one patch after the highest reserved tag.
The candidate and canonical candidate state advance to v0.5.45 while release.json and previousRelease remain v0.5.42.
Regression tests prove a Draft-reserved v0.5.44 requires v0.5.45 and that the diagnostic does not imply Draft publication.
The v0.5.44 tag and Draft Release remain untouched, and no external publication is performed.

The plan records the lifecycle cycle, user-authorized same-PR recovery exception, and mandatory future recovery sequence: record failure, repair the gate, advance to the next reserved patch, complete PR lifecycle, then retry publication.
guidelines: Preserve fail-closed release validation and immutable tag boundaries.
Keep published release truth separate from reserved tag sequence truth.
Use a narrowly documented recovery exception only when an archived predecessor PR is blocked by the corrective candidate metadata itself.
Do not claim v0.5.44 is publicly released.

intent.problem: PR #401 repairs Draft asset verification but its template-smoke gate fails because the remote highest semantic tag is already the immutable, unpublished v0.5.44 Draft tag while next-release.json still names v0.5.44. The checker calls that tag an accepted previous release, obscuring that the public baseline remains v0.5.42 and creating a lifecycle cycle: the corrective PR cannot merge until the next candidate advances.
constraints: Preserve the immutable v0.5.44 tag and Draft Release.
Advance the candidate only to v0.5.45; retain v0.5.42 as the published baseline and basedOnReleaseTag.
Do not publish externally in this Work Item.
Record the same-PR recovery exception and the durable process rule in the plan.
Retain PR checks, archive evidence, and branch cleanup requirements.
intent.rationale: An immutable tag reserves its semantic version whether its associated Release is Draft or published. Separating reserved-tag progression from published-release truth makes the required v0.5.45 correction explicit, prevents reuse of a failed tag, and allows the corrective PR to regain a valid candidate without rewriting historical evidence.

rawUserRequest: The next candidate is v0.5.45. Adding it to archived, unmerged #401 is acceptable; what matters is fixing the process so this does not keep happening in the future.
